name: Saint Frances of Rome
history: A Roman noblewoman who wanted to be a nun but was married at twelve, and became a saint as wife, mother and widow. Through plague, war and the deaths of two of her children she nursed the sick and fed the poor of Rome. She founded the Oblates of Tor de’ Specchi and is said to have seen her guardian angel.
life: Francesca Bussa de’ Leoni was married to Lorenzo Ponziani, of a rich Roman family, and lived with her husband for forty years in deep affection. With her sister-in-law Vannozza she visited hospitals, nursed the sick and gave away food from the family stores, to the anger of her father-in-law until, tradition says, the granary was found full again. Rome was torn by the Great Schism and occupied by the troops of Ladislas of Naples; the Ponziani lost their property, Lorenzo was wounded and their son Battista was taken hostage. Two of her children died in plague years. In 1425 she founded a community of women living under the Benedictine Olivetans, without enclosure, serving the poor of the city. When Lorenzo died in 1436 she joined them as superior. She is the patron of motorists, from the tradition that her angel lit her way at night.
prayerTo: Saint Frances, you sought God in the chapel and found Him also in the kitchen, the sickroom and the streets of Rome. Pray for wives, mothers and widows, for families in hardship, and for me, that I may serve God faithfully in the duties of my state of life. Amen.
penance: When a household duty interrupts your prayer today, leave the prayer gladly and do it well. Give some food to a food bank in honour of Frances.
meditation: She was often called away from prayer by her family, and tradition says that once she came back to find the page she had left written in gold. Which interruption today is God’s?
